claims.text: HfNbTaTiZr can remain a single-phase bcc refractory high-entropy alloy in the proposed operating regime.
The random-solid-solution state has high lattice distortion and mass disorder.
The low thermal conductivity of the random-solid-solution state is dominated by phonon scattering from mass variance.
Thermal annealing can induce and percolate Hf-Nb- or Ta-Ti-rich SRO clusters without causing phase separation.
A moment tensor or comparable machine-learning potential can represent the chemical energetics needed to evolve SRO.
The alloy remains single-phase bcc from 800 K to 1500 K.
An SRO correlation length exceeding the phonon mean free path permits percolative thermal-transport pathways.
A percolating SRO network creates a distinct phonon-dispersion landscape with reduced group velocities inside SRO regions.
SRO-cluster boundaries form continuous low-scattering pathways that act as a phonon wire.
Thermal transport is governed by competition between mass-disorder scattering and connectivity of the SRO network.
Percolating SRO changes the phonon density of states and phonon group velocities rather than acting only as discrete scattering obstacles.
The SRO force-constant distribution may support lower-frequency, higher-velocity modes or reduce the scattering cross-section of dominant heat-carrying modes.
Connected SRO clusters allow phonons to bypass the strongly scattering random matrix.
Reaching the SRO percolation threshold produces a sharp, nonlinear increase or saturation in thermal conductivity rather than a monotonic decrease.
The resulting thermal conductivity is significantly higher than predictions from series/parallel mixing rules or mass-variance alloy-scattering models.
The proposed effect requires chemically distinct but structurally coherent SRO clusters and fails below the percolation threshold.
The proposed effect fails if SRO causes phase separation or transformation to intermetallic phases.
The cited literature does not directly observe the effect of SRO on phonon group velocity in bcc refractory alloys.
The cited high-entropy-carbide evidence shows that mass disorder destabilizes vibrational entropy.
Correlating APT or PDF measurements of SRO length with thermal-conductivity and phonon-dispersion measurements can test for a percolative transition.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis attributes the transition to percolation of low-velocity modes, the structural mediator places reduced velocities inside SRO regions but transport along cluster boundaries, and the mechanism alternatively invokes higher-velocity modes within connected clusters. These are materially different descriptions of the proposed conducting pathway.
The headline permits either an increase or saturation, whereas the predicted outcome calls for a sharp nonlinear increase. Saturation alone would not necessarily satisfy the sharper prediction.
